learning: Iteration 8 (mass 0.4 kg) gave the best score at 71.37 and confirmed that yaw inertia was a real constraint. Every track still ends at max_error 0.062-0.066 m with about one line loss per run on the curves. The remaining untested lever is ground speed, so this iteration isolates wheel_radius with the controller held fixed.
notes: Iteration 8 geometry with wheel_radius reduced from 0.030 to 0.025 m, as the Builder requested, to lower ground speed. The controller is unchanged from iteration 8 so the speed effect is isolated. Watch oval progress, which should fall, and max_error on the s-bend and slalom, which should drop toward 0.06 m.
rationale: Iteration 8 (mass 0.4 kg, track 0.08 m, kd 0.30) is the best result so far at 71.37. Every track still ends off track with max_error about 0.062-0.066 m, just past the fixed 0.06 m floor, and the s-bend and slalom still lose the line about once per run (0.95-1.0 events). The Builder's requested change is wheel_radius 0.030 to 0.025 m, which lowers ground speed for the same PWM demand. That is the only untested lever with a plausible path to holding the floor, since mass, track, lead, span and footprint have been exhausted. I therefore keep the iteration 8 geometry and change only wheel_radius, so any shift in outcome is attributable to speed. The controller is kept identical to iteration 8 (base_speed 1.5, kp 1.25, ki 0, kd 0.30, weights [2.0, 1.3, 0.7, 0, -0.7, -1.3, -2.0], last_direction). Changing gains now would confound the speed test. Expected: max_error at or below about 0.06 m on the s-bend and slalom, line-loss events falling toward 0, and steering oscillation no higher than about 0.17. Progress on the oval is likely to fall, because the robot covers less ground per second. The race will show whether that trade is worth it.
